title: I'm building an Mario Super Sluggers like game using Tripo, Suno, Astra and Opus 5.5.
author: eon95
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I'm a solo developer working on **Super Epic Sluggers**, an arcade-style baseball game inspired by games like Mario Super Sluggers.

I've been developing it in Unity, and AI tools have been a big part of making the project possible as a solo dev.

My current workflow includes:

* **Tripo** for generating base 3D models.
* **Suno** for creating the soundtrack.
* **ChatGPT Astra and Opus 5.5** for UI artwork, card designs, and visual concepts.

I'm combining those assets with my work on the gameplay, animations, and game systems.

One thing I'm focusing on is making everything feel visually consistent, rather than looking like a collection of unrelated AI-generated assets.

I put together a video showing the game and its progress so far:

[https://youtu.be/6mlUWKcIU34](https://youtu.be/6mlUWKcIU34)

I'd love some honest feedback, especially from other developers using AI in their workflows.

Still plenty of work ahead, but I'm excited about where it's going!

comments.author: TheMedicineMan-
comments.body:
I tried a baseball game as well.  The most challenging aspect, as I'm sure you've noticed, is sports animations.  AI isn't capable so unless you have animating skills you're likely going to struggle.

I did have success taking swing animations from other games, but obviously this can't be released commercially.  I shelved my game for now due to the animations not being up to par. 

If you're making this game for you and some buddies to have fun - solid.  If you're trying to release this commercially, then there is a long way to go in the animation department.  If I were you, I'd focus on ironing out your animations before continuing any other work.

replies.author: eon95
replies.body:
I’ve been wanting to this for years but for exactly that reason I’ve never attempted it because I can code, I can model props and whatnot but I can’t animate to save my life. But with how much these AI models have evolved I decided to see how well they could do with that. 

Surprisingly it exceeded what I thought they could do, currently all animations used are either from Mixamo or the model created it in Blender. Obviously they’re not to the standard for a comercial release but for a vertical slice I think they are fine.

I have tried Cascadeur for a different game I was working on and I was able to actually create pretty decent animations so If I decide to keep working on this, I might try that to see how it does. Maybe you can check that out too for your game?

Thanks for the feedback!

replies.author: TheMedicineMan-
replies.body:
Yep, I went through a few research iterations to find what the best was. I was able to generate a pretty smooth swing from Mixamo but it took a good day of iterating.  Once I got batting I started to move to the other aspects and realized the amount of animations needed for the game I was going for, arcade baseball but different trajectory then you, it just wasn't going to work.

  
I'm in the same boat as you, 10+ year as a software engineer but no modeling/animation/game dev experience.  I got really close to where I wanted with modeling but animations were too jarring for me so I pivoted on a different game.  That being said, I did consider just moving forward with development with the believe that by the time I finished my feature work for v1 the AI models/market would have progressed for models/animations enough for my use case.
